headline: Shah tells UN floods killed at least 1,400, asks 3 more years to keep trade breaks
dek: Nepal Wire could not verify the toll Shah cited, and he proposed a Nepal, India and China glacier monitoring mechanism neither neighbour has answered.
body_markdown:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah landed at Tribhuvan International Airport on Saturday afternoon after addressing the United Nations for the first time as head of government. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Home Minister Sudhan Gurung and Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Khadak Raj Paudel received him at the airport, according to Radio Nepal Online.

UN News described the floods as a "Himalayan Tsunami" in its coverage of the speech. Shah told the Assembly the floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, according to UN News, the world body's own reporting service. He put recovery needs at roughly 10 percent of Nepal's gross domestic product, a figure the Kathmandu Post also carried from his prepared remarks. Nepal Wire cannot verify the death toll independently. It is Shah's own figure, stated from the podium.

The speech matters to Nepalis beyond New York. Nepal remains formally scheduled to leave the Least Developed Country category in November 2026 unless the General Assembly approves the extension, a change that would end trade preferences and concessional aid that exporters and the government currently depend on. Shah told the Assembly the floods make that timeline unworkable and pressed for more time.

## LDC graduation, a vote away

Nepal already has a recommended extension in hand. The UN Committee for Development Policy recommended a three year extension to November 2029, and the Economic and Social Council referred the matter to the UN General Assembly for a final decision, UNB reported in July 2026. That vote, not Shah's speech, is what will decide the timeline exporters and the government are watching.

In New York, Shah pressed the case directly to Secretary-General António Guterres in a bilateral meeting. Guterres offered condolences over the floods and repeated the UN's solidarity with Nepal, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs note carried by Nepalnews. Neither the ministry's account nor other outlets Nepal Wire reviewed describe a firm UN commitment to grant the delay.

Shah also proposed what he called a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, led jointly by Nepal, India and China, to share satellite data, monitor glacial lakes and build early warning systems across the range, according to the text of his address published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Kathmandu Post's transcript coverage. He argued Nepal produces less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions yet bears an outsized share of the damage, a figure repeated in the ministry's press note. Nepal Wire could not independently verify this figure against a global emissions database.

## No response yet from India or China

Neither Indian nor Chinese officials have publicly responded to the proposal, and no outlet Nepal Wire reviewed reports any commitment from either government. The mechanism remains a proposal Shah put on the table, not an agreement.

Shah also called for climate finance to come as grants rather than loans through the UN's Loss and Damage Fund, and invoked the principle that richer nations bear greater responsibility for emissions, language drawn from his prepared remarks. He held a separate bilateral meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Nepalnews reported, without giving further detail on what was discussed.

Not everyone at home is convinced the speech will change much. A Kathmandu Post column published the same week questioned whether the address amounts to more than words. The column argued the speech alone will not decide whether India, China or the Loss and Damage Fund act.

What happens next depends on the General Assembly. No General Assembly decision had been reported as of Sunday, September 27.

key_facts.fact: PM Balendra Shah returned to Kathmandu on Saturday, September 26, and was received at Tribhuvan International Airport by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Home Minister Sudhan Gurung and Minister Khadak Raj Paudel, according to Radio Nepal Online.

Shah told the UN General Assembly the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, a figure he stated himself and Nepal Wire could not independently verify.
Nepal formally asked the UN Committee for Development Policy in May to delay its LDC graduation from November 2026 to November 2029.

The UN Committee for Development Policy recommended a three year extension of Nepal's LDC graduation to November 2029, and the Economic and Social Council referred the matter to the UN General Assembly for a final decision, UNB reported in July 2026.
Shah proposed a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism led by Nepal, India and China to share satellite data and monitor glacial lakes.
Shah raised the LDC graduation delay with UN Secretary-General António Guterres in a bilateral meeting; Guterres offered condolences but no outlet reported a firm UN commitment.

ranking.reason: A head of government policy story with primary records behind it: the Kathmandu Post transcript and the MoFA press note. The LDC graduation extension request affects trade and aid for millions, and Saturday's return keeps it inside the window. Shah's 1,400 death figure must be attributed to him, and the Himalayan Mechanism must not be presented as agreed by India or China. Domestic skepticism about substance should be included.

Confirmed at rank 3. Primary records support it: the Kathmandu Post transcript and the MoFA press note. The LDC graduation extension request affects trade and aid, and Saturday's return keeps it inside the window. Attribute the 1,400 toll to Shah and say that India and China have not publicly responded to the mechanism.

findings.passage: The UN Committee for Development Policy has not yet ruled on the 2029 delay request, and no timeline for a decision has been reported.
findings.problem: This is out of date and appears wrong. Public reporting from as early as July 2026 shows the CDP already assessed Nepal's request and recommended a three year extension, and that ECOSOC referred the matter to the General Assembly for a final decision. The article tells readers the CDP has not ruled at all, which understates how far the process has moved and gives a false picture of what happens next.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the status: report that the CDP recommended a three year extension to 2029, that ECOSOC referred the matter to the UN General Assembly, and that the General Assembly's final vote or note is what remains pending. Cite the CDP recommendation and the ECOSOC referral with dates.

findings.passage: He called the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods a "Himalayan Tsunami"
findings.problem: The phrase appears in a UN News headline describing the floods, but the transcript excerpts available describe the disaster in different words, for instance calling it 'a warning to the world.' It is not confirmed that Shah himself used the exact phrase 'Himalayan Tsunami' from the podium rather than this being UN News's own framing of the event.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the full transcript from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or UNDP for the exact phrase. If Shah did not say it himself, attribute the label to UN News rather than presenting it as his direct quote.

findings.passage: Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal accompanied Shah on the trip
findings.problem: Multiple outlets reviewed, including the Kathmandu Post and Nepalnews reporting on the LDC request, spell the foreign minister's name 'Shisir Khanal,' not 'Shishir Khanal.' House style requires keeping names spelled as the outlet spells them, and a spelling mismatch on a sitting minister's name is an easy accuracy fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the minister's preferred Latin script spelling from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and use it consistently throughout.

findings.passage: PM Balendra Shah returns from UN summit
findings.problem: The event was the UN General Assembly's high level week, not a 'summit' in the formal sense used for gatherings like the G20 or COP. Calling it a summit is loose and could confuse readers about what kind of event this was.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'UN General Assembly' or 'UN General Assembly's high level week' instead of 'summit' in the headline.

findings.passage: The UN Committee for Development Policy has not yet ruled on the 2029 delay request, and no timeline for a decision has been reported.
findings.problem: Because the CDP to ECOSOC to General Assembly process is already advanced, the article's framing of the LDC delay as an open question Shah is fighting for from scratch misses the more relevant and more reportable angle for readers: Nepal's exporters and government already have a recommended extension in hand, and the real remaining question is a General Assembly vote, likely with a nearer term date than the article implies.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe the LDC section around the actual live procedural step, the General Assembly's pending action, since that is what readers with a stake in trade preferences need to track next.

findings.passage: PM Balendra Shah returns from UN summit, urges climate justice and LDC delay
findings.problem: The headline buries the sharpest number, the 1,400 dead and 6,000 missing figure, which is the most shareable and human fact in the piece. 'LDC delay' is policy jargon most readers will not click on.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead the headline with the flood toll or the trade preference stakes, for example: 'Shah tells UN floods killed 1,400, asks for three more years before Nepal loses trade breaks.'

findings.passage: Nepal Wire cannot verify the death toll independently. It is Shah's own figure, stated from the podium.
findings.problem: This hedge is good practice and should stay, but the dek states the death toll as a flat fact ('Nepal's floods killed at least 1,400 people') without the same attribution signal a reader gets in the body. A reader who only sees the dek gets an unattributed casualty figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add attribution in the dek itself, for example 'Shah told the UN General Assembly Nepal's floods killed at least 1,400 people, a toll Nepal Wire could not independently verify.'

findings.passage: He argued Nepal produces less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions yet bears an outsized share of the damage, a figure repeated in the ministry's press note.
findings.problem: This emissions figure is attributed only to the ministry's own press note repeating Shah's claim, with no independent source such as a global emissions database cited or checked against, even though such data is publicly available and would let Nepal Wire confirm or correct the number rather than just relay it.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the figure against a standard source such as Our World in Data or the Global Carbon Project and either confirm it independently or keep the same explicit 'Nepal Wire could not verify' hedge used for the death toll.

red_team.summary: The article is carefully sourced on the flood toll and speech content, with commendable hedging on the death toll, but it gets the single most checkable fact in the piece wrong: the CDP has already recommended a three year LDC graduation extension and the matter sits with the General Assembly, not the earlier stage the article describes. That error also flattens the story's real news value, since the live question is a General Assembly vote rather than an open CDP decision. Smaller issues include an unverified direct quote attribution for 'Himalayan Tsunami,' a likely minister name spelling mismatch, and a headline that buries the sharpest number in favor of policy jargon.

responses.response: The red team's evidence is specific and dated, and it points to a real gap in our reporting. The CDP to ECOSOC to General Assembly pipeline is the standard graduation process, and if CDP already recommended the 2029 extension and ECOSOC referred it up, our line that the CDP has not ruled at all is stale and misleads readers about how close Nepal is to actually getting the delay. We should have checked the CDP's own site and ECOSOC records before publishing that line, not just relied on the absence of a ruling in the outlets we reviewed.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the closing paragraph's status line with: 'The UN Committee for Development Policy recommended a three year extension to 2029, and the Economic and Social Council referred the matter to the UN General Assembly for a final decision. No date has been reported for that General Assembly vote.' Cite the CDP recommendation and ECOSOC referral directly, with dates, alongside the existing Kathmandu Post May 22 source.

responses.response: We cited UN News for the 'Himalayan Tsunami' phrase but presented it in the body as something Shah himself said from the podium, without checking the primary transcript we also have listed as a source. If the phrase is UN News's own headline framing rather than a direct quote, we have misattributed language to a named public official, which is exactly the kind of attribution slip the house style guide warns against.
responses.proposed_edit: Cross check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs transcript and UNDP text for the exact phrase. If Shah used it verbatim, keep it as a quote with a citation to the transcript. If he did not, rewrite as: 'UN News described the floods as a "Himalayan Tsunami" in its coverage of the speech, in which Shah said...' and attribute the casualty language directly to his remarks instead.

responses.response: House style is explicit that we keep names spelled as the outlet spells them, and we have a documented mismatch against the Kathmandu Post's spelling of the foreign minister's name. This is a low cost, high value fix for a sitting official's name.
responses.proposed_edit: Change 'Shishir Khanal' to 'Shisir Khanal' throughout the article, matching the Kathmandu Post spelling, unless the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website uses a different Latin script spelling, in which case use that instead.

responses.response: The gathering was the UN General Assembly's high level week, not a summit in the sense readers would expect from events like the G20 or COP. It is a small imprecision, but house style asks for specific, checkable language in the headline, and 'summit' invites readers to assume a different kind of gathering.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the headline to: 'PM Balendra Shah returns from UN General Assembly, urges climate justice and LDC delay'

responses.response: This follows directly from f1. Once we correct the process status to show the CDP already recommended the extension and ECOSOC referred it to the General Assembly, the more useful angle for readers with a stake in trade preferences is the pending General Assembly vote, not a request Shah is making from a standing start.
responses.proposed_edit: Rewrite the closing section to lead with: 'Nepal already has a recommended three year extension in hand. The UN Committee for Development Policy backed the 2029 delay, and the Economic and Social Council referred it to the General Assembly. That vote, not Shah's speech, is what will decide the timeline exporters and the government are watching.'

responses.response: House style asks headlines to lead with a real claim or number rather than a teaser, and our current headline leads with a routine travel fact, 'returns from UN summit,' before the actual news. The flood toll and the trade stakes are both more specific and more consequential than 'urges climate justice.'
responses.proposed_edit: Change the headline to: 'Shah tells UN Nepal's floods killed 1,400, asks for three more years before losing trade breaks'

responses.response: The dek states the death toll as flat fact with no attribution signal, while the body carefully attributes it to Shah and flags it as unverified. A reader who only reads the dek gets a different standard of care than a reader who reads the body. That inconsistency is a real fairness gap, not just a stylistic one.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the dek to: 'Shah told the UN General Assembly Nepal's floods killed at least 1,400 people, a toll Nepal Wire could not independently verify, and pitched a Himalayan monitoring pact with India and China.'

responses.response: We relayed the 0.1 percent emissions figure only from the ministry's press note, which is itself just repeating Shah's own claim, and we did not check it against an independent emissions database even though one is publicly available. This is a fixable gap given house style's demand that every number trace to a source we can stand behind, not just a source we can cite.
responses.proposed_edit: Check the figure against a standard source such as the Global Carbon Project or Our World in Data. If it holds up, add that source alongside the ministry note. If it does not check out cleanly, add the same explicit hedge used for the death toll: 'Nepal Wire could not independently verify this figure.'

defense.summary: Seven of the eight findings identify real gaps between what our sources actually show and what the article states, and the defense accepts all of them. The most serious is f1: the article tells readers the LDC graduation timeline is still an open question Shah is fighting for, when the more advanced procedural status described by the red team, if accurate, would mean Nepal already has a recommended extension awaiting a General Assembly vote. That single correction also drives the fix for f5. The remaining accepted findings are smaller attribution and precision fixes, a possibly misattributed quote, a minister's name spelling, an imprecise word in the headline, a missing attribution signal in the dek, an unverified emissions figure, and a headline that could lead with a sharper fact. None of the findings were contested because each pointed to a genuine, checkable shortfall rather than a matter of house style preference or reasonable editorial judgment we can defend as written.

rulings.note: The closing status line is stale. The red team cites dated reporting that the CDP recommended a three year extension and ECOSOC referred the matter to the General Assembly. As written, the article misstates the live process. High severity, but one pass can fix it.

UN News used the phrase in its headline. The Kathmandu Post takeaways headline suggests Shah may have said it, but that is not confirmed. The article must cite the MOFA transcript or attribute the label to UN News.
The spelling of a sitting minister's name must match the outlet or ministry spelling. The accompaniment claim is also not traced to any listed source.
Loose wording. The replacement headline under f6 resolves it.
This follows from f1. The pending General Assembly action is the step exporters and readers need to track.
The toll and the trade stakes should lead the headline. The defence's proposed headline runs about 95 characters, over the 90 limit, and drops 'at least', so a corrected version is specified below.
The dek states an unverified casualty figure as flat fact. The defence's proposed dek runs about 190 characters, over the 160 limit, so a shorter version is specified below.
The article already frames the figure as Shah's argument, so it is properly attributed under rule 2. An independent check is welcome but not required to publish.

required_edits: Headline: replace with 'Shah tells UN floods killed at least 1,400, asks 3 more years to keep trade breaks' (about 83 characters).

Dek: replace with 'Nepal Wire could not verify the toll Shah cited, and he proposed a Nepal, India and China glacier monitoring mechanism neither neighbour has answered.' Keep it one sentence under 160 characters.

Paragraph 1: attribute the airport reception to Radio Nepal Online, the source listed in key_facts and sources. Remove the attribution to a 'Ministry of Foreign Affairs press note reported by Nepalnews' unless Nepalnews actually carries it. Delete 'four days after he left Kathmandu' unless a listed source gives the departure date.

Paragraph 2, 'Himalayan Tsunami': check the MOFA transcript at the listed mofa.gov.np URL. If the phrase appears verbatim, keep the quote and cite the MOFA transcript. If it does not, rewrite as: UN News described the floods as a "Himalayan Tsunami" in its coverage of the speech. Shah told the Assembly the floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing.
Paragraph 3: change the scheduled graduation sentence to say Nepal remains formally scheduled to leave the LDC category in November 2026 unless the General Assembly approves the extension.

LDC section and closing: replace 'The UN Committee for Development Policy has not yet ruled on the 2029 delay request, and no timeline for a decision has been reported.' with: The UN Committee for Development Policy recommended a three year extension to 2029, and the Economic and Social Council referred the matter to the UN General Assembly for a final decision, UNB reported in July. Give the date of the CDP recommendation and of the ECOSOC referral as the source states them. Before publishing, confirm whether the General Assembly has already acted. If no action is reported, write: No General Assembly decision had been reported as of Sunday. Add the UNB article URL to the sources list, and add any CDP or ECOSOC primary record you use.

Reframe: open the LDC section by stating that Nepal already has a recommended extension and that the General Assembly's action decides the timeline exporters are watching. Present Shah's speech and the Guterres meeting as pressing that case.
Himalayan mechanism paragraph: delete 'and the UN Development Programme', which is not in the sources list. Attribute the mechanism text to the MOFA transcript and the Kathmandu Post transcript.

Kathmandu Post column paragraph: delete 'a reminder that strong applause in New York does not settle' because applause is unsourced and the phrasing echoes a banned phrase. Rewrite as: The column argued the speech alone will not decide whether India, China or the Loss and Damage Fund act. Paraphrase only what the column says.

Final paragraph: use the MOFA website spelling of the foreign minister's name. If MOFA gives none, use the Kathmandu Post spelling. Keep 'accompanied Shah on the trip' only if a listed source reports it, and add that source. Otherwise cut the sentence. Delete 'will likely field the follow up questions', which is speculation. End on the pending General Assembly step instead.
judge_1.reason: The piece handles the unverified flood toll and the absence of Indian and Chinese responses well. But it misstates the core LDC process, which is the article's most checkable fact, and it carries attribution slips: an unconfirmed quote, an airport source mismatch, an unlisted UNDP source and unsourced lines about Khanal. All of these can be fixed in one pass, and a sharper headline and dek will lift its reach.

findings.passage: Neither Indian nor Chinese officials have publicly responded to the proposal, and no outlet Nepal Wire reviewed reports any commitment from either government.
findings.problem: The first clause states an absolute negative as established fact (no Indian or Chinese official has responded) rather than as a limit of Nepal Wire's own review. Absence of evidence in outlets Nepal Wire checked does not prove Indian or Chinese officials have said nothing anywhere, including in bilateral or diplomatic channels not covered by English-language wire coverage. This is a claim the paper does not actually own.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'No outlet Nepal Wire reviewed reports a public response from Indian or Chinese officials to the proposal, and none describes a commitment from either government.' Drop the standalone absolute claim.

findings.passage: Shah tells UN floods killed at least 1,400, asks 3 more years to keep trade breaks
findings.problem: The headline implies Shah personally asked the UN podium for '3 more years.' The transcript excerpts Nepal Wire's own sources quote (MOFA, Kathmandu Post transcript, UNDP) show Shah's speech language on graduation is about urgency and the timeline being unworkable, not a specific '3 years' ask stated from the podium. The three-year figure comes from the CDP recommendation process described later in the piece, a separate track from the speech itself. Presenting it as something Shah 'asked' the UN in his address conflates two different actions.
findings.suggested_fix: Adjust headline or body to make clear the 3 year figure is the CDP's recommended extension (already pending before the General Assembly), and that Shah's UN remarks argued the graduation timeline is now unworkable, without implying he specified '3 years' from the podium unless a source shows he did.

findings.passage: UN News described the floods as a "Himalayan Tsunami" in its coverage of the speech.
findings.problem: UN News's own reporting attributes the phrase to how the disaster's ferocity 'many have called' a Himalayan Tsunami, echoing language from Shah's own prepared remarks, not an independent UN News characterization. The article presents it as if UN News coined or independently applied the label, which overstates the outlet's role and blurs where the phrase originated.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify origin: 'Shah's prepared remarks described the floods with a ferocity many have called a "Himalayan Tsunami," a phrase UN News also used in its headline.'

findings.passage: He argued Nepal produces less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions yet bears an outsized share of the damage, a figure repeated in the ministry's press note.
findings.problem: The 0.1 percent figure traces directly to the text of the address itself as published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and multiple outlets carrying the full transcript, not to a separate 'press note' distinct from the speech text. Calling it a press note figure understates that this is Shah's own stated line from the podium.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'a figure from the text of his address, published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' rather than attributing it to a press note.

findings.passage: Shah told the Assembly the floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, according to UN News, the world body's own reporting service.
findings.problem: The qualifier 'the world body's own reporting service' is imprecise. UN News is editorially independent of the political organs of the UN even though it is a UN department; describing it this way could be read as implying the death toll carries UN institutional endorsement, when it is simply UN News reporting what Shah said.
findings.suggested_fix: Simplify to 'according to UN News' and drop the descriptive clause, since the body already separately notes Nepal Wire could not verify the toll.

findings.passage: Prime Minister Balendra Shah landed at Tribhuvan International Airport on Saturday afternoon after addressing the United Nations for the first time as head of government.
findings.problem: The lead opens with a routine arrival detail rather than the striking flood toll or the trade preference stakes that the headline promises. Readers who click on '1,400 dead' and 'trade breaks' land on an airport reception paragraph before getting the payload, undercutting the hook.
findings.suggested_fix: Open with the death toll and GDP damage figure Shah cited at the UN, then move the airport reception detail to a later paragraph.

findings.passage: "image": {"kind": "found", "credit": "Photo: \u201cU.N. General Assembly Hall New York (NY) April 2016 (27131089892)\u201d by Ron Cogswell..."
findings.problem: The chosen image is a generic, empty 2016 UN hall photo unrelated to this speech or Shah's appearance. Multiple outlets (NepYork, Kathmandu Post) show contemporaneous photos of Shah addressing the Assembly, which would better carry the story even though usage rights would need checking.
findings.suggested_fix: Look for a rights-clear photo of Shah at the podium or of Nepal's delegation at the session rather than a stock, unrelated hall interior.

findings.passage: Not everyone at home is convinced the speech will change much. A Kathmandu Post column published the same week questioned whether the address amounts to more than words.
findings.problem: This is an opinion column being cited as if it represents a broader domestic consensus ('not everyone at home is convinced'), when only one column is named. The framing overstates the breadth of skepticism from a single data point.
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute the skepticism specifically to the column rather than implying wider domestic sentiment, e.g. 'One Kathmandu Post columnist questioned whether the address amounts to more than words.'

red_team.summary: The article is carefully hedged on the hardest number (the 1,400 death toll) and correctly separates the LDC extension recommendation from Shah's speech, which is good practice. But it makes one unsupported absolute negative claim about Indian and Chinese silence, slightly misattributes the origin of the 'Himalayan Tsunami' phrase to UN News rather than the speech itself, and its headline compresses a multi step bureaucratic process into an ask Shah did not clearly make from the podium. It is highly relevant to Nepali and diaspora readers given the trade and aid stakes, but the lead buries the strongest facts under an airport arrival and leans on a generic stock photo, both of which cost it shareability.}

responses.response: The red team is right. Stating 'neither Indian nor Chinese officials have publicly responded' as a flat fact oversteps what we can actually confirm. We only know what our reviewed outlets show. The claim should be scoped to our own reporting, not asserted as a universal negative.
responses.proposed_edit: Neither Indian nor Chinese officials have publicly responded to the proposal, according to outlets Nepal Wire reviewed, and none of those outlets describe a commitment from either government.

responses.response: The headline compresses two separate tracks into one action. The 3 year figure comes from the CDP recommendation already pending at the General Assembly, not a number Shah stated from the UN podium. As written, the headline implies Shah asked the Assembly for '3 more years' in his speech, which our own sourcing does not support. This needs fixing to keep the two tracks distinct.
responses.proposed_edit: Shah tells UN floods killed at least 1,400, presses case for pending 3 year trade break extension

responses.response: Fair catch. Our phrasing credits UN News with coining or independently applying 'Himalayan Tsunami,' when the outlet is echoing language describing the disaster's ferocity that traces back to characterizations around Shah's own remarks. We should make the origin clearer.
responses.proposed_edit: Shah's prepared remarks described the floods with a ferocity many have called a "Himalayan Tsunami," a phrase UN News also used in its coverage of the speech.

responses.response: Correct. The 0.1 percent emissions figure traces to the text of the address itself, published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and carried in transcript coverage. Calling it a 'press note' figure is an unnecessary and inaccurate layer of attribution when the address text is the actual source.
responses.proposed_edit: He argued Nepal produces less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions yet bears an outsized share of the damage, a figure from the text of his address, published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

responses.response: The description risks reading as institutional endorsement of the toll even though the following paragraph clarifies Nepal Wire could not verify it. Since the caveat already does the necessary work, the descriptive clause about UN News's status is extra and can be cut without losing anything.
responses.proposed_edit: Shah told the Assembly the floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, according to UN News.

responses.response: House style calls for opening with the strongest verified fact and explaining why it matters early. The airport arrival is true and sourced, but it buries the toll and the trade stakes the headline promises. Reordering serves both the reader and the style guide.
responses.proposed_edit: Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations General Assembly the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, a figure Nepal Wire could not independently verify. He put recovery needs at roughly 10 percent of Nepal's gross domestic product. Shah landed at Tribhuvan International Airport on Saturday afternoon after the address, received by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Home Minister Sudhan Gurung and Minister Khadak Raj Paudel, according to Radio Nepal Online.

responses.response: The current image is honestly captioned as a found, generic UN hall photo with clear CC BY 2.0 licensing. Swapping to a photo of Shah at the podium from NepYork or Kathmandu Post would require verifying usage rights we do not currently have confirmed, and using an outlet's photo without clearance risks a worse problem than a generic but accurately labeled stock image. We should not trade a verified license for an unverified one on a virality guess.
Right. We named one columnist but wrote as if it reflected broader domestic sentiment. That overstates the evidence we actually have, which is a single column.

defense.summary: Six of eight findings are accepted, mostly small attribution and precision fixes: scoping the India/China silence claim to our own review, separating the CDP's 3 year recommendation from what Shah actually said at the podium, clarifying the origin of the 'Himalayan Tsunami' phrase, correctly sourcing the 0.1 percent emissions figure to the address text rather than a press note, trimming an unnecessary descriptive clause about UN News, reordering the lead to foreground the toll and stakes per house style, and not generalizing one columnist's skepticism into broader domestic sentiment. The image finding is contested because the current photo carries a verified license and replacing it with an outlet's photo of unverified rights would trade a real problem for a bigger one.

rulings.note: The body states Indian and Chinese silence as a universal fact. The dek repeats it as 'neither neighbour has answered.' Nepal Wire can only own what its reviewed outlets show. The defence accepted this, but no revision pass remains to scope both passages.

Nepal's formal May request did target 2029. But the body says only that Shah 'pressed for more time.' No cited source shows him naming three years from the podium, so the headline's 'Shah tells UN ... asks 3 more years' outruns the body. Medium severity.
UN News attributes 'Himalayan Tsunami' to what many have called the disaster. The article presents it as UN News's own characterisation, which misattributes the phrase.
The 0.1 percent figure comes from the address text published by MOFA. Crediting it to a 'press note' adds a wrong attribution layer. Low severity.
'The world body's own reporting service' is an accurate description of UN News. The next sentences state plainly that the toll is Shah's figure and unverified, so no endorsement is implied.

House style requires opening with the strongest verified fact. The lead is an airport reception, while the headline sells a death toll and trade stakes. This drags virality below the newsroom's 60 floor.
The defence is right. A correctly licensed CC BY 2.0 image beats an outlet photo with unconfirmed rights. Generic art is a weakness, not an error.
One named column does not support 'not everyone at home is convinced' as a description of wider sentiment. The skepticism should be attributed to the single columnist.
